stories.title: Fears grow that US will put Nobel-winning judge under sanctions after Myanmar genocide ruling
bullet_points: A ruling against Myanmar could set precedent for court’s judgment on Israel’s actions in Gaza  Fears are growing that the US could impose sanctions on judges at the international court of justice, including this year’s  Nobel peace prize winner, Navi Pillay , if the  court rules on Thursday that the Myanmar government committed genocide  against the Rohingya.

The ICJ has never found a state responsible for committing genocide, and a significant factor in previous cases has been how to prove “intent” in a crime defined as acts committed with the “intent to destroy, in whole or in part” a national, ethnical, racial or religious group.

stories.title: Florida pastor found guilty over 2021 assassination of Haitian president
bullet_points: Christian Emmanuel Sanon faces life in prison after conviction on charges arising from killing of Jovenel Moïse  A Florida pastor with dual Haitian-American citizenship was convicted on Wednesday of US charges arising from the 2021 assassination of the Haitian president Jovenel Moïse.
Christian Emmanuel Sanon was found guilty on charges including conspiring to kill Moïse after a nearly eight-week trial in federal court in Miami.
He had faced a total of eight charges including conspiracy to kidnap or kill a person outside the United States.

stories.title: Hegseth uses Venezuela visit to boast of Maduro’s capture by US military
bullet_points: Defense secretary asserts US dominance on trip that would have seemed ‘impossible, almost unbelievable’ a year ago  Pete Hegseth has used his first visit to Venezuela since US special forces abducted its former president, Nicolás Maduro, to boast of the dictator’s capture during what he called “the single most sophisticated military operation in the history of Latin America”.

Maduro was controversially seized by Delta Force operatives in the early hours of 3 January, setting in motion an improbable rapprochement between Washington and Venezuela’s anti-imperialist “Chavista” regime, which has ruled since 1999.

stories.title: European Commission accused of sugarcoating figures to release funds to Egypt
bullet_points: Leaked documents raise questions about claims Egypt met welfare targets to qualify for €2.5bn in loans  The European Commission has been accused of sugarcoating figures to enable it to release funds to Egypt under a landmark pact with the authoritarian government of Abdel Fatah al-Sisi.
The charge relates to a €7.4bn deal  promised by Ursula von der Leyen , the European Commission president, to al-Sisi on a high-profile visit to Cairo in 2024.

The three-year “strategic and comprehensive partnership” was intended to bolster Egypt’s shaky economy, deter migrants from coming to Europe and shore up a region reeling from the 7 October attacks and Israel’s war on Gaza.

stories.title: Caribbean nations fear economic impact of shuttering citizenship program after EU threats
bullet_points: St Kitts and Nevis to wind down citizenship-by-investment program after EU warns of end to visa-free access  The decision by St Kitts and Nevis to end a lucrative programme offering citizenship to wealthy foreigners in exchange for investment threatens its economy and ability to support people in need, the premier of the island of Nevis has warned.

On Friday, Terrance Drew, the prime minister of the twin-island Caribbean nation, announced he would wind down the citizenship-by-investment (CBI) programme, after the European Union threatened to end visa-free access for St Kitts and Nevis.

According to the NGO Survival International, members of the Awá people, who live in voluntary isolation, arrived on Monday in a village and made contact with a government team in a “historic encounter”.

Representative Juan Vargas shared a photograph of the boy and his family in a social media post on Monda, writing: “11 days ago, an 8-year-old in San Diego was taken into federal custody during an immigration check-in.
He was separated from his loved ones and held in a facility in Texas.

stories.title: Five EU states announce plans for immigration ‘return hubs’ in Rwanda
bullet_points: Germany, Austria, Netherlands, Denmark and Greece likely to face challenges to policy criticised as ‘grave moral failing’  Five EU member states have announced plans to set up an offshore centre in Rwanda for people with no legal right to stay in Europe, in a pilot scheme that is expected to face legal challenges and has been denounced as “a grave moral failing”.

The five countries – Germany, Austria, the Netherlands, Denmark and Greece – are the first to seek to use the EU’s  newly agreed returns law  that allows   people who have exhausted all avenues of appeal against their removal from Europe to be sent to a third country.

stories.title: Race to replant five South African baobabs after export blocked
bullet_points: The trees, intended for an unnamed buyer in Georgia, were reportedly dug up without the necessary permits  Environmentalists in South Africa are racing to replant five centuries-old baobabs after the 20-tonne trees were dug up by an exporter, who tried to ship them thousands of miles to Georgia.
The baobabs arrived at a reserve in Timbavati, in north-eastern South Africa, on Wednesday, where they will be replanted and supported by cables to help them recover.
The trees had been stranded at a warehouse in Durban since July, when they were intercepted by authorities who said they had been moved without the necessary permissions.
